title: Resource Management with use

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Resource Management with use** as part of **Exceptions, Files, and Input/Output**. Close closeable resources on every exit path; Kotlin’s `use` pattern makes cleanup explicit and dependable. Use the subtopics—The use Function, Resource Cleanup, Handling Cleanup Failures—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Real projects depend on reliable error handling, modular organization, reproducible builds, and safe language boundaries. This lesson helps turn isolated syntax into maintainable applications.

items.text: The use Function describes how behavior is declared, passed, or composed. Make inputs and return types clear, keep side effects visible, and use a small call-site example to judge readability.

items.title: Handling Cleanup Failures
items.text: Handling Cleanup Failures helps make behavior observable and repeatable. Define the expected result, include a boundary or failure case, and preserve enough diagnostic information to locate the cause without leaking sensitive data.
